mechanics.name: Built to Last
mechanics.currentEffect: While in a Locker with a depleted Item, after 14/12/10 seconds by perk tier restore its Charges to 99% of maximum. Each subsequent use restores 66%, then 33%. Can be used a maximum of 3 times per Trial.
activation: Enter a Locker with a depleted Item.
Ends/deactivates when: Each recharge ends when its tier time has elapsed or the interaction is interrupted.
Ends/deactivates when: Cannot be used after three activations.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (9.1.0): Final 9.1.0 live notes set the time spent in a Locker to 14/12/10 seconds; this differs from the 12/10/8-second PTB value.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: After 14/12/10 seconds by perk tier, a Locker recharge restores a depleted Item to 99%; later activations restore 66% and then 33%, up to 3 uses per Trial.
duration: First recharge after 14/12/10 seconds by tier; restores 99%.
Second use restores 66%; third use restores 33%.
mechanics.tokenOrStackBehavior: Uses are limited to 3 per Trial; recharge amount declines from 99% to 66% to 33%.
specialInteractions: The recovered Item Charges are based on the held Item's maximum.

editorial.summary: Recharge a depleted Item in a Locker up to three times, restoring 99%, then 66%, then 33% of its maximum Charges.
useCases: Extend strong Toolboxes across multiple generators instead of exhausting them in one burst.
Turn high-quality Med-Kits into repeated healing resources throughout the Trial.
Recharge Flashlights or other limited Items when their utility is central to the build.
counters: Requires the Item to be depleted and costs 10 seconds in a Locker at Tier III for each recharge.
The restored percentage drops on each successive use.
A weak Item remains a weak Item even when you receive more Charges.
pros: Can multiply the total value of a strong Item several times over.
Works with multiple Item categories rather than one narrow strategy.
Predictable and easy to execute once the Item is depleted.
cons: Requires bringing or finding an Item worth recharging.
Locker downtime can erase part of the gained efficiency.
Third recharge is much smaller than the first.
analysis: Built to Last earns this position because Items are some of the strongest resources Survivors can bring, and the perk effectively stretches those resources far beyond their normal charge limit. A first recharge to 99% is especially powerful with a high-quality Toolbox or Med-Kit that was already optimized with Add-ons.

The perk becomes more impressive when the Item itself creates time savings. Recharging a Toolbox costs Locker time, but the restored charges can accelerate generators later. Recharging a Med-Kit can create additional independent heals. The correct question is not whether ten Locker seconds are free; it is whether the restored Item produces more strategic value than those seconds cost.

Its flexibility also matters. Built to Last is not locked to generators or healing, and it can support Flashlight-focused players as well. That makes the perk a resource multiplier whose exact role changes with the Item equipped, which is useful for players who already build intentionally around their inventory.

It stays below the stronger universal perks because the slot is only as good as the Item being recycled. A player who enters with a poor Item, loses it, or never needs its extra Charges gets limited value. With premium equipment, however, Built to Last can quietly produce a huge amount of additional match resources.
editorial.verdict: A powerful Item multiplier whose ceiling depends on what you bring. Built to Last turns premium gear into a much deeper resource pool, at the cost of deliberate Locker downtime.
